correctness.rationale: Four-set parity with the designated anchor forces every old triple from the descendant graph. For a fresh point, the n−1 binary triple values involving the anchor freely determine the other new triples by the same parity rule. Realize each pattern by odd graph-edge parity after adding a vertex not adjacent to the anchor; ultrahomogeneity and the extension property identify these patterns exactly with complete nonalgebraic types over the named base. The grade counts the anchor incidents plus the switched edges off the anchor, giving the claimed polynomial and 2^(n−1) types. Every labelling of an isomorphic two-graph is obtained by choosing an anchor and permuting its complement, so orbit marking is exact. The independent replay uses actual triple relations to mark all anchored labels and applies four-set parity directly to all extension profiles. It obtains class counts 1,1,2,3,7,16,54,243, with as many grades through seven and 219 at eight, split 198/18/3 by fibre sizes 1/2/3. All 21 catalogue fibres (45 members) match in masks, coefficients and incidences; distinct incidence sequences within every nontrivial fibre establish refined reconstruction. The three specified masks have the displayed polynomial, degrees and pairwise distinct Seidel characteristic polynomials.
residual_risks: Uploaded code was inspected, not executed. The replay independently checks the quotient, every certificate and the spectral witness.
No injectivity or separation statement for parameter orders above eight is established.

evidence: The replay finds 42 ordinary Ising pairs among 1,044 unlabelled seven-vertex graphs; in every pair the two isolated-anchor extensions are in different two-graph orbits. Thus a prior seven-vertex ordinary Ising pair, as cited by the frozen record, transports to a genuine eight-point type-polynomial collision. For example masks 6581 and 6827 yield orbit minima 6549 and 6827 respectively. This computation establishes the implication without attributing particular masks to the inaccessible article.

Across all anchor representatives these ordinary pairs give 21 distinct unordered two-graph pairs out of 27, touching 18 of the 21 nonsingleton fibres and fully accounting for 17. They do not recover all collisions. The prior spectral table also groups differently.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Credit the prior Ising mechanism for producing eight-point failures; in particular the ordinary-edge-count mismatch of the three chosen descendants is not evidence that their unpointed classes cannot be connected by a change of anchor to ordinary Ising collisions. The complete enumeration, exclusion of smaller-order two-graph collisions and incidence separation are separate claims not mechanically supplied by prior Ising examples or the ambient two-graph tables.

evidence: On n labelled vertices, the allowed extension incidence graphs form the coset E+Cut(K_n) over F₂, with each cut counted once (opposite subsets give the same cut). The grade is the edge Hamming weight. Equivalently this is the signed complete-graph zero-field Ising edge-disagreement distribution, with the spin-global-flip factor removed.

For the ordinary graph G obtained by deleting the isolated anchor, a cut S contributes grade |E(G)|+|S|+|S|(n−1−|S|)−2e_G(S,complement S). The ordinary bivariate Ising cut distribution therefore determines this polynomial for the pointed representative, though not conversely.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A switch-class weight-spectrum or signed complete-graph equivalent table would be material. The ordinary Ising distribution computes the type polynomial by collecting classes of cuts, but is not itself that invariant on unpointed two-graphs. On seven-vertex G the edge total is already determined by the singleton-cut coefficients, so equal ordinary Ising polynomials imply equal anchored type polynomials.

originality.rationale: The supported distinction is the full small-order reconstruction and exact eight-point fibre classification of the coefficient enumerator, and the incidence refinement that separates all ambiguous classes. The two-graph list and switching formalism are classical. Ordinary Ising equivalence of seven-vertex graphs does transfer to examples of collisions after adjoining an isolated anchor; this is genuine partial coverage, not a novel source of all eight-point counterexamples. The independent comparison of all ordinary seven-vertex cut-distribution fibres gives at most 21 of the 27 unordered colliding two-graph pairs by this transfer and does not give the sharp lower-order injectivity or the incidence refinement. No inspected source gives the full distinct result.
residual_risks: Andrén–Markström full text was not lawfully accessible by the tried routes, so its exact examples and any further signed-complete-graph analysis were not assessed directly; the transfer comparison does not assume those details.
A prior full switching-coset weight census under an alternative name could affect priority; the bounded evidence cannot exclude it.

value.rationale: The grade naturally measures the number of triples created by a fresh point in a two-graph. The exact finite boundary and full fibres quantify the information loss from replacing named triple profiles by their sizes; neither cospectrality nor ordinary Ising equality alone describes the collisions. The incidence refinement recovers precisely the reconstruction lost at the first threshold. This is a complete small-order reconstruction result, not a recomputation of the known ambient count or an arbitrary coefficient slice.
residual_risks: The refinement's sufficiency is established only at the stated small orders; the useful new result is not the mere existence of a transported Ising collision.
